name: Ouroboros Energy Thermal Regulation Core
description: The Thermal Regulation Core is a deep-body augmentation — a palm-sized thermoelectric management unit implanted in the upper abdominal cavity, interfaced with the body's circulatory and endocrine systems via a network of micro-catheter heat exchangers routed through major arterial pathways. Developed originally for Ouroboros Energy's deep-geothermal extraction crews who operated in environments exceeding 60°C for extended shifts, the Core can actively suppress or amplify the body's heat production and dissipation, maintaining core temperature within a 0.3°C variance regardless of external conditions ranging from -40°C to +85°C. It draws power from a compact thermoelectric cell that converts the body's own temperature differential into supplemental energy.

cultural_context: Ouroboros Energy originally distributed the Core as occupational equipment to its extraction crews, which means there is a generation of retired industrial workers in Meridian 88's outer districts walking around with military-grade thermal suppression implants they received as part of their employment package. This has created an odd black-market ecosystem where former Ouroboros workers sell calibration access to their units to operatives who can't afford the licensed version. Among corporate security, detecting a Core on a scan and finding it registered to an energy sector retiree is a known red flag.
known_users: Assassins and infiltrators requiring IR invisibility
Survivalist communities in Meridian 88's industrial heat zones
story_hooks: A decommissioned Ouroboros extraction site is being repurposed, and the company is quietly trying to recover all Core units issued to former crew — some of those workers don't want to give them back.
Someone has been using a Core's 'dead biometric' feature to fake their own death repeatedly, collecting on multiple life insurance policies across different corporate jurisdictions.
A new firmware update is being pushed to all licensed Cores — but the update includes a remote-access backdoor that Ouroboros hasn't disclosed to users or regulators.
A series of murders has been committed by someone who doesn't appear on any thermal surveillance — the only lead is a calibration technician who services unlicensed Core units.
